published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'In this paper we obtain the first ‘absolute’ QEI for the minimally-coupled massive quantum Klein–Gordon field on four dimensional globally hyperbolic spacetimes; that is, a bound which depends only on the local geometry ... Moreover, the bound is explicit and can be formulated covariantly under additional (general) conditions. We also generalise our results to incorporate adiabatic states.' Intro (p.3): 'For averaging along timelike worldline γ, our result takes the form ∫ dt f²(t)⟨v^a v^b T^ren_ab⟩_ω(t) ≥ −B_A, (5) where B_A = ∫_{R+} dξ/π [f⊗f ϑ* T^split H̃]^(−ξ,ξ) + “local curvature terms” (6)'. Precise statement, Theorem 3.1 (p.18): 'Let Σ be a small sampling domain of dimension n in (M,g) with hyperbolic coordinate map κ and suppose Q is a partial differential operator of order at most one with smooth real-valued coefficents in a neighbourhood of Σ. Set k = max{n+3, 5}. For any real-valued f ∈ C∞_0(Σ) and any Hadamard state ω we have the inequality ∫_Σ dvol f² (Q⊗Q(Λ_ω − H_2))(x,x) ≥ −B > −∞ (64)', B given by (65). Remarks (p.18): 'This bound depends nontrivially on the coordinates (and on any partition of unity used to reduce a general timelike submanifold into small sampling domains).' Worldline form (p.23, eq. 82): ∫ dτ f²⟨u^a u^b T^ren_ab⟩_ω(γ(τ)) ≥ −∫_{R+} dξ/π [|h_κ|^{1/4} f ⊗ |h_κ|^{1/4} f ϑ* T^split H̃_5]^(−ξ,ξ) + ∫ dτ f² (Q + u^a u^b C_ab)|_γ(τ), with T^split built from 'any smooth tetrad ... such that e_0 = u on γ' (81). Renormalisation (p.8): 'any remaining finite renormalisation must take the form of a state-independent conserved local curvature term C_ab that vanishes in Minkowski space' (eq. 21: ⟨T^ren⟩ = ⟨T^fin⟩ − Q g_ab + C_ab); 'We take the view that the tensor C_ab is a necessary part of the specification of a given species of scalar field ... Given sufficient experimental accuracy C_ab should, in principle, be measurable.' Flat check (p.24, eq. 88): massless, Minkowski, inertial curve: '∫ dt f²(t)⟨u^a u^b T^ren_ab⟩_ω(γ(t)) ≥ −(1/16π³)∫_{R+} dη |f̂(η)|² η⁴ (88) which is the same as the QEI for the massless field in Minkowski spacetime obtained in [9]' [Fewster & Eveson 1998]. Then: 'on small length scales one expects the massive quantum field in a curved background to behave like its massless counterpart in flat spacetime ... This will be investigated in a future work.' Non-minimal (p.8): 'A similar problem arises for the non-minimally coupled scalar field. In this case one must smear the stress-energy tensor even to obtain an inequality on the classical field [21], which necessitates a more complicated analysis at the quantum level [22].'
published_hypotheses: H1 field: minimally coupled Klein-Gordon, (∇²+μ²)φ = 0, mass μ ≥ 0 (p.4); free field, algebraic quantisation with CCR (p.4)
H2 spacetime: four-dimensional, smooth, Hausdorff, paracompact, no boundary, Lorentzian (+,−,−,−), globally hyperbolic (p.4); c = ℏ = 1
H3 states: Hadamard states (Thm 3.1, p.18); widened by Thm 3.3 (p.25) to adiabatic states of order N > 9/2

H4 sampling: a SMALL SAMPLING DOMAIN (p.17-18): Σ contained in a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood AND covered by one hyperbolic chart with bounded coordinate speed of light (62); for the worldline: 'provided that the track of γ can be contained in a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood in M' (p.23); otherwise a partition of unity over a compact subset, on which the bound then depends (p.18)
H5 smearing: real-valued f ∈ C∞_0 (compact support), weight f²; smooth timelike worldline in proper-time parametrisation (geodesic NOT required); tetrad with e_0 = u on γ (81)

H6 renormalisation: Hadamard point-splitting with Wald's w_0 = 0, length scale ℓ, conservation term −Q g_ab, residual C_ab state-independent, conserved, local curvature, vanishing in Minkowski (p.5 fn 2, p.6, p.8); C_ab is part of the specification of the field species

H7 bound form: partial sums H̃_k of the Hadamard series, k = max{n+3,5} (H̃_5 on a worldline), plus ∫ f² (Q + u u C_ab); finite (Thm 3.1 part three); reference-state-free (p.21); coordinate- and (in some cases) tetrad-dependent, covariant only under restrictions shown for worldvolume averages with Fermi normal coordinates (p.18, p.25-27)
H8 eq. (88) specifically: massless, Minkowski, inertial worldline along the time axis, where the full Hadamard series is its leading term (p.23)

later_literature.what: Restates FS's small sampling domain definition verbatim-in-substance ('Following Ref. [20] we define a small sampling domain Σ ... contained in a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood ... single hyperbolic coordinate chart'), and states its own non-minimal NEC bound 'is for a difference QEIs unlike the absolute one that was possible for the minimally coupled field' and state-dependent. As of 2023 the absolute form remains minimal-coupling only in this line of work; confirms H4 is part of how the field uses FS.

Defines an 'absolute' QEI as one whose lower bound 'depends in a local and covariant way on the spacetime metric and the test function'. FS's general Theorem 3.1 bound is chart/tetrad dependent and covariant only under restricted sampling (FS p.18, 25-27), so 'absolute' in the review's stricter sense attaches to FS only under those restrictions; supports the drift entry on 'depends ONLY on local geometry'.
At C = 0 the F&T double integral equals FS (86)/(88) identically (K6), confirming the tree's 'same form and constant' claim.

lacked_data: FS is a theorem of mathematical physics; its conclusion uses NO measured datum, so M's hypothesis ('previous physicists may have lacked certain data') has no empirical input to act on for the theorem itself. What the authors lacked in 2007, by their own statement: (i) control of the scale on which the curved-spacetime bound is approximated by the Minkowski massless bound (88) -- 'This will be investigated in a future work' (p.24), 'ongoing work' (p.27); this is missing ANALYSIS, not data, and it bears on the tree's wording at throatmass.py:85-87 ('gap ... narrow'), not on any tree verdict; (ii) a value of C_ab, which FS say 'should, in principle, be measurable' (p.8); the bound's EXISTENCE and FORM do not move with it, but any number obtained by evaluating (82) on the corridor moves additively by INT f^2 u u C_ab -- the tree already carries C_ab as an unevaluated term, so O2's evaluation, if ever run, is DATA-DEPENDENT on C_ab. Evidence either way: the finite, closed-form parts (84)-(88) re-derive exactly (11/11 checks), and the flat constant agrees with Fewster-Eveson (via the 9/64 Lorentzian ratio, matching the tree's independent fixture) and with F&T (5.6) at C = 0; the one discrepancy found, (87)'s missing 1/pi in the text layer, does not propagate to (88). The later papers read (FO 2007, FFKP 2023, Kontou-Sanders 2020) restate FS's scope without correcting it. Whether a C_ab measurement or a small-scale-approximation theorem appeared later was NOT-SEARCHED (alphaXiv quota).
grade_evidence: The theorem stands as published: the flat check re-derives exactly (rederive K1-K6, 11/11 pass), the tree's quotes at qeihps.py:63-72 are verbatim to pp.1 and 8, and the core use -- an absolute, reference-state-free lower bound on the Hadamard-renormalised energy density along a worldline exists for the minimally coupled KG field of mass >= 0 in 4D globally hyperbolic spacetimes, so throatmass.py's 'no QEI can bound rho_ren' is correctly DEMOTED -- is accurate. It is NARROWED because the tree states it on a larger class than FS prove: (a) the Hadamard-state hypothesis of Thm 3.1 (p.18) is dropped at fewsterteo.py:113-121/177-179, specthm.py:2146-2153, ledger.py:1819-1820 (carried at qeihps.py and O5); (b) the small-sampling-domain hypothesis (worldline track inside a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood, p.17-18, p.23) is dropped at every owner and weakened to 'a causal diamond suffices' in qeihps.py; (c) 'depends ONLY on local geometry' drops the body's coordinate/tetrad/partition-of-unity dependence (p.18, p.25); (d) the residual in B_A is C_ab AND the Q term, with (88) a Minkowski special case whose approximation to the curved bound FS leave to future work (p.24, p.27), against throatmass.py:85-87's 'gap is real but narrow'. None of these moves a tree verdict (O2 stays OPEN and unevaluated; O5's demotion stands), and no moved datum moves the conclusion. The (87) text-layer factor-pi discrepancy is recorded, not graded: (86)->(88) holds.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners' statements carry Thm 3.1's hypotheses as FS state them -- Hadamard (or adiabatic N > 9/2) state, small sampling domain (or an explicit partition of unity), chart/tetrad dependence, the Q + C_ab term -- and throatmass.py:85-87 drops 'narrow' or cites a result that controls the curved-vs-flat difference. To WRONG: a computed counterexample to Thm 3.1 or to (88) (none found; K1-K6 agree). To DATA-DEPENDENT: if the tree ever evaluates (82) on the corridor, the number moves with C_ab (unmeasured).
